title: Global AI and Digital Summit in Seoul holds ministerial as 60 nations join
subtitle: The World Bank's first AI summit held outside the United States convened its ministerial meeting in Seoul today, with policy forums, hackathon winners, and 60 national delegations in attendance.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: The Global AI and Digital Summit opened in Seoul on October 19, 2026 and runs through October 22, co-hosted by the World Bank Group and the Government of the Republic of Korea. On October 21, Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon and World Bank Vice President for Digital and AI Kim Sang-bu co-chaired the summit's AI and Digital Ministerial meeting. Officials from roughly 60 nations, along with development partners, private-sector leaders and researchers, were on the attendee list, per Korea Times.

The summit is the first of its kind held outside the United States, which is a deliberate signal from the World Bank: AI development policy is not an OECD-plus-China conversation. Program sessions this week include policy forums on grid and compute access, procurement in low-income countries, and the AI-and-development track that absorbed yesterday's Small AI for Development Hackathon. Three winning teams from that World Bank hackathon — picked from applicants aged 18 to 35 — were slated to present their projects at today's ministerial session.

The practical question hanging over the week is whether these gatherings produce enforceable commitments or just communiqués. The 2024 UN General Assembly resolution on AI, adopted by consensus, had no binding mechanism. The OECD's 2024 Principles update is non-binding by design. Seoul is early in a track that is still mostly declarative, but holding it under the World Bank's flag, with ministers in the room, puts development-finance leverage next to the words — the next test is whether loan terms or capacity-building commitments actually follow.

For learners: pay attention to who hosts the AI governance meetings, not just who attends. A summit at the UN is a norms conversation; a summit at the World Bank is a money conversation. If your work touches public-sector AI, grant funding, or deployments in developing economies, the venue tells you which lever — persuasion or purse — is actually being pulled this cycle.
